# Problem 1

## Load Track Data
```{r}
track <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EricBrownTTU/ISQS5346/main/menstrack.csv")
head(track)
```

## a. Summary Statistics for 100m and 200m Dash
```{r}
summary_stats <- function(x) {
  list(
    Mean = mean(x),
    Median = median(x),
    Variance = var(x),
    Std_Dev = sd(x)
  )
}

stats_100 <- summary_stats(track$m100)
stats_200 <- summary_stats(track$m200)

print(stats_100)
print(stats_200)
```

## b. Mode Value Commentary
*The mode is not analytically useful here because the data are continuous times and not likely to repeat. Therefore, mode does not provide meaningful insight in this context.*

## c. Z-scores and Outliers
```{r}
z_scores_100 <- scale(track$m100)
z_scores_200 <- scale(track$m200)

# Most extreme observations:
extreme_100 <- track[which.max(abs(z_scores_100)), ]
extreme_200 <- track[which.max(abs(z_scores_200)), ]

print(extreme_100)
print(extreme_200)
```
*Observations with the highest absolute z-scores may be considered potential outliers.*

## d. Correlation Matrix
```{r}
track_subset <- cbind(track$m100, track$m200, track$m3000)
colnames(track_subset) <- c("m100", "m200", "m3000")

cor_matrix <- cor(track_subset)
print(cor_matrix)
```
*We observe a stronger correlation between 100m and 200m, which makes sense as they are both sprint events. The 3000m event shows a weaker correlation with sprints.*

# Problem 2

## Load Exit Survey Data
```{r}
survey <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EricBrownTTU/ISQS5346/main/pgs.csv")
head(survey)
```

## a. Contingency Table
```{r}
table_fac_col <- table(survey$FacTeaching, survey$COL)
print(table_fac_col)
```

## b. Proportion Table
```{r}
prop_table <- prop.table(table_fac_col)
print(prop_table)
```

## c. P(ED and Rating = 4)
```{r}
print(prop_table["4", "ED"])
```

## d. P(College = BA)
```{r}
print(sum(prop_table[, "BA"]))
```

## e. P(Rating = 2)
```{r}
print(sum(prop_table["2", ]))
```

## f. P(Rating = 3 | College = AS)
```{r}
print(prop_table["3", "AS"] / sum(prop_table[, "AS"]))
```

## g. P(College = VPA | Rating = 5)
```{r}
print(prop_table["5", "VPA"] / sum(prop_table["5", ]))
```

## h. Teaching Quality Comparison (BA vs ED)
```{r}
barplot(table_fac_col[, c("BA", "ED")], beside = TRUE, legend = TRUE,
        col = c("lightblue", "pink", "orange", "green", "purple"),
        main = "Teaching Ratings: BA vs ED", ylab = "Count")
```
*You can interpret from the chart whether BA or ED had better teaching ratings based on the distribution.*

# Problem 3

## a. Expected Number of Heads (All Fair Coins)
```{r}
x <- expand.grid(c1 = c(0,1), c2 = c(0,1), c3 = c(0,1), c4 = c(0,1), c5 = c(0,1))
expected_heads <- mean(rowSums(x))
print(expected_heads)
```

## b. Simulate 10,000 Coin Flips
```{r}
set.seed(123)
results <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = 10000, ncol = 5))
results[,1] <- sample(c(0,1), 10000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(4/5, 1/5))
results[,2] <- sample(c(0,1), 10000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(3/5, 2/5))
results[,3] <- sample(c(0,1), 10000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(2/5, 3/5))
results[,4] <- sample(c(0,1), 10000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1/5, 4/5))
results[,5] <- sample(c(0,1), 10000, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0, 1))

heads_count <- rowSums(results)
head(heads_count)
```

## c. Histogram of Heads Count
```{r}
hist(heads_count, main = "Histogram of Number of Heads", xlab = "Number of Heads",
     col = "skyblue", breaks = 5)
```
*There are no outcomes with 0 heads because coin 5 always shows heads.*

## d. Bayes' Theorem: P(Coin = 4 | Head)
```{r}
head_counts <- colSums(results)
total_heads <- sum(head_counts)
prob_coin4_given_head <- head_counts[4] / total_heads
print(prob_coin4_given_head)
```
